newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian merger activity surged in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Canadian merger activity surged in quarter.

text.p: Canadian mergers and acquisitions forged ahead in the first quarter, with real estate, consumer products and energy leading the pack, a report by merchant bank Crosbie & Co Inc said on Tuesday.

The M&A Quarterly Report said that in the quarter Canadian firms made 327 deals worth C$24 billion, the second highest transaction value on record. In the year-earlier period, 251 mergers and acquisitions worth C$22 billion were unveiled.

Transactions in the real estate sector rose by 107 percent, driven by TrizecHahn's aggressive hunt for U.S. and European office towers. Consumer products gained 105 percent. Oil patch mergers climbed by 88.5 percent.

The red-hot energy sector, still rife with takeovers after a banner 1996, yielded C$4.85 billion in announced transactions during the first quarter. Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd's C$1.6 billion offer for Wascana Energy Inc topped the energy merger list.
Abitibi-Price Inc's planned union with Stone-Consolidated Corp, valued at C$4.1 billion, was the biggest overall merger revealed in the quarter.

Cross-border activity also rose over the year-ago period. In the first quarter of 1997, companies based in Canada revealed plans for 72 foreign acquisitions, 20 percent above the first three months of last year. These foreign targets were in the U.S. 60 percent of the time.
A total of 36 Canadian companies found themselves in the sights of foreign acquirers during the period, 29 percent above the 28 similar deals announced in the 1996 quarter.
